meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'удобно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Вчера как-то неудобно у нас получилось.
examples.trans: Things turned out rather awkwardly between us yesterday.

examples.text: Мне жутко неудобно.
examples.trans: I feel terribly awkward.

examples.text: Здесь очень неудобно сидеть.
examples.trans: It is very uncomfortable to sit here.

meanings.en: to turn out, to work out
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лучиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'turned out', paired with 'получаться'.

examples.text: Катя, не слушай его, он хотел получить деньги!
examples.trans: Katya, do not listen to him, he wanted to get money!

examples.text: Всё получится!
examples.trans: It will all work out!

examples.text: Из него получится хороший врач.
examples.trans: He'll make a good doctor.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('needed').

examples.text: Тебе нужны деньги, а мне нужна дочь.
examples.trans: You need money, and I need my daughter.

examples.text: Слушайте, парни, мне очень нужна ваша помощь.
examples.trans: Listen, guys, I really need your help.

examples.text: Мне ещё работа нужна.
examples.trans: I need a job too.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'money' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Час гоняешь, потом весь день перебираешь.
examples.trans: You ride for an hour, then overhaul it all day.

examples.text: А за моржа весь день мусор выносишь.
examples.trans: And for the walrus comment, you are taking out the trash all day.

examples.text: Тебе нужны деньги, а мне нужна дочь.
examples.trans: You need money, and I need my daughter.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning '(our) daughter' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Тебе нужны деньги, а мне нужна дочь.
examples.trans: You need money, and I need my daughter.

examples.text: А у тебя ещё дочки есть?
examples.trans: Do you have any more daughters?

examples.text: Немедленно оставь мою дочь в покое!
examples.trans: Leave my daughter alone immediately!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'understood', paired with 'понимать'.

examples.text: Ты уберёшь свою машину прямо сейчас, понял?
examples.trans: You are going to move your car right now, got it?

examples.text: Понял, а сколько здесь денег?
examples.trans: Got it, and how much money is here?

examples.text: Понял, ты думаешь, сразу нести шашлык?
examples.trans: Got it, do you think I should bring shashlik right away?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'колько'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Понял, а сколько здесь денег?
examples.trans: Got it, and how much money is here?

examples.text: Эй, герой, сколько тебя ещё ждать?
examples.trans: Hey, hero, how much longer do we have to wait for you?

examples.text: Сколько жвачки!
examples.trans: So much gum!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Здесь вообще-то люди ходят.
examples.trans: People actually walk through here.

examples.text: Понял, а сколько здесь денег?
examples.trans: Got it, and how much money is here?

examples.text: Здесь ровно сто тысяч рублей.
examples.trans: There is exactly one hundred thousand rubles here.

examples.text: Здесь ровно сто тысяч.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'hundred', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У меня такой в мастерской стоит.
